title: Add quantization execution metrics tags (profile id/version, mode, kernel path)
author: Logan Wright
body:
Summary: This PR adds consistent tags to traces and metrics so we can segment latency/cost/error dashboards by quantization execution path. Specifically, we emit (a) the resolved quantization profile id + version, (b) execution mode (baseline vs quantized vs fallback), and (c) kernel path (which quant kernel family/impl actually ran) across the runtime request lifecycle and billing attribution pipeline.

Motivation: Route-level quantization enablement needs safe rollout/rollback + alerting. Today we can tell overall token cost/latency moved, but we cannot reliably answer: which routes are executing quantized vs baseline? which profile version is live? are we seeing fallbacks due to incompatibility? which kernel path correlates with the regression? These tags unlock: (1) per-route quantized-vs-baseline comparisons, (2) quick identification of mis-scoped profiles, (3) SRE alerts on fallback/error rate spikes, and (4) billing/cost attribution breakdowns by profile.

Scope:
- Server-side tracing: attach quantization metadata to the top-level request span and to the internal "inference" child span.
- Metrics: add low-cardinality tags to existing counters/histograms (no new metric names unless needed).
- Cost attribution: extend the execution-mode tag through the usage record so Console can show quantized vs baseline spend.
- Fallback observability: make fallback explicit (and reason-coded) instead of inferred from missing profile tags.

Non-goals:
- No customer-facing API surface changes.
- No new route config logic (handled in ENG-18451 / PR 28792).

Tag definitions (authoritative):
- quant.exec_mode: one of ["baseline", "quantized", "fallback"]
  - baseline: quantization not requested or not eligible
  - quantized: quant profile resolved + compatible + quant kernels executed
  - fallback: quantization requested/selected but runtime executed baseline kernels (due to incompatibility, missing artifact, runtime guardrail, etc.)
- quant.profile_id: stable profile identifier (e.g., "qpl:meta-llama/Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct:int4")
- quant.profile_version: semantic version (e.g., "1.2.0")
- quant.kernel_path: kernel implementation family (low-cardinality), e.g. ["awq", "gptq", "marlin", "cutlass_int8", "baseline"]
- quant.fallback_reason (only when exec_mode=fallback): one of ["gpu_arch_mismatch", "kernel_unavailable", "artifact_missing", "sequence_length_unsupported", "profile_invalid", "guardrail_triggered"]

Where we emit:
- Tracing:
  - span: request.root (gateway -> runtime boundary)
  - span: inference.execute
  - span: kv_cache.prefill (optional; only emits exec_mode + kernel_path)
- Metrics:
  - runtime.request.latency_ms (histogram): add quant.exec_mode, quant.kernel_path
  - runtime.inference.tokens_out_total (counter): add quant.exec_mode, quant.profile_id (sampled), quant.profile_version (sampled)
  - runtime.inference.errors_total (counter): add quant.exec_mode, quant.fallback_reason
  - billing.usage.tokens_billed_total (counter): add quant.exec_mode (NOTE: profile_id/version intentionally NOT propagated into billing events yet; see "Cardinality" below)

Cardinality + safety notes:
- quant.profile_id + quant.profile_version can be high cardinality if emitted on every metric. To avoid exploding time series, we:
  - Always tag traces with full profile_id/version (trace sampling already applies).
  - Emit full profile_id/version on metrics only for a small set of "review" metrics and behind sampling (default 1%).
  - Always emit quant.exec_mode + quant.kernel_path on metrics (bounded enum set).
- quant.kernel_path is intentionally a small enum; we map internal kernel identifiers into a stable set and log the full internal identifier only in structured logs.

Implementation details:
- Added QuantizationExecutionContext (runtime/telemetry) that is created after profile resolution and passed through execution + attribution.
- Standardized the tag keys (constants) to prevent drift between runtime spans and statsd/otel exporters.
- Updated attribution pipeline to include exec_mode (but not profile_id/version) in the usage record.
- Added a unit test suite to validate: (1) baseline path emits baseline tags, (2) quantized path emits profile_id/version, (3) fallback path emits fallback_reason, and (4) tag enums remain stable.

Testing:
- Unit: telemetry tag contract tests.
- Integration: replayed synthetic traffic with quantization flag enabled on a canary route and confirmed Console dashboards can segment by exec_mode.
- Perf: validated no measurable overhead at p95 under 1k rps due to tag computation (strings are interned; mapping is constant-time).

Rollout plan:
- Land tags in runtime first (this PR).
- Enable dashboards/alerts in a follow-up (SRE/Console).
- During beta: alert on runtime.inference.errors_total{quant.exec_mode="fallback"} and on fallback_reason != "gpu_arch_mismatch" (unexpected).

Docs / runbooks:
- Internal: updated telemetry tag registry comment blocks with quant.* keys.
- External docs: none in this PR.

Related:
- ENG-18472 Cost attribution for quantized path
- PR 28805 fallback to baseline on incompatibility
- PR 28792 route policy enablement flag
commits: telemetry: add quantization tag constants + enum mapping
runtime: plumb QuantizationExecutionContext through execute path
metrics: tag request latency + tokens + error counters with exec_mode/kernel_path
tracing: attach quantization metadata to request + inference spans
billing: propagate exec_mode into usage record; add compatibility test coverage
tests: add contract tests for baseline/quantized/fallback tagging
review_conversation:
Nadia Rahman: For billing attribution, do we really want profile_id/version in usage records? That seems like it could explode dimensions in downstream reporting.
Logan Wright (author): Agree; this PR only propagates exec_mode into usage records. Full profile_id/version stays in traces + sampled metrics. Added a note in the PR body and a guard to prevent accidentally adding profile_id/version to billing tags.

Caleb Johnson: Please ensure the tag keys are consistent between spans and metrics. Today we have both quant.profile and quant_profile floating around.
Logan Wright (author): Good catch. Replaced all ad-hoc keys with constants in runtime/telemetry/quantization_tags.ts and updated span enrichment accordingly.

Mateo Alvarez: For fallback, can we surface the reason? We had a past incident where mismatched GPU arch caused a spike and it took too long to confirm.
Logan Wright (author): Added quant.fallback_reason (bounded enum) on error counters and on inference span. Also logs include full internal kernel id and compat check details.

Allison Grant: Cardinality risk: emitting profile_id on tokens_out_total even at 1% could still be noisy on very high volume. Can you make sampling configurable and default to off in prod until dashboards are ready?
Logan Wright (author): Updated: sampling defaults to 0% in prod, 1% in staging/dev, controlled via TELEMETRY_QUANT_PROFILE_TAG_SAMPLE_RATE. exec_mode/kernel_path remain always-on.

Allison Grant: Approved once sampling default is 0% in prod.
Logan Wright (author): Done. Pushed commit "billing: default sampling off in prod".

Nadia Rahman: Approved.
Caleb Johnson: Approved.
Mateo Alvarez: Approved.
Allison Grant: Approved.
release_notes: Internal-only: Added quantization execution tags to traces/metrics (exec mode, kernel path; profile id/version on traces and sampled metrics). Enables dashboards/alerts for route-level quantization rollouts.
merge_outcome: Merged to main via squash; will ship behind existing quantization feature flags.
